Two birotor robots join forces as a four-propeller aerial platform

IEEE Spectrum’s weekly video collection features connected flying robots alongside humanoids, unusual locomotion and automated laboratories.

IEEE Spectrum ↗18 September 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1Videos 14

A weekly collection of robotics videos

IEEE Spectrum’s Video Friday gathers demonstrations from multiple research and development teams. A highlight is a pair of connected two-propeller flying robots from CLIMB Lab, alongside developments in humanoids and automation.

Movement and working near people

The collection includes Digit 5 and work from Figure, as well as NYU’s WorMa. That robot transfers water between its front and rear to shift its weight distribution and help it negotiate obstacles.

A broad range of research

Other projects include an underwater quadruped, MIT’s automated optics laboratory and NASA’s Lunabotics competition, where students test robotic vehicles in simulated lunar-surface conditions.

How to read the collection

This is a set of videos from different projects, rather than a test of one product. Technical details and experimental results should be checked against the development teams and materials referenced by the original article.
